entry.title: Not decided: a second, lower-memory attempt on 12 Oct also needed more memory than our shared machine has (about 3 GB at its peak; the machine allows 3 GB for everything running on it). Measured: it ran out while preparing the moving-edge test input, before the first simulation step (sampled peak about 3.17 GB of the 3.22 GB limit). No result in either direction, no ledger row, no chart; the 10 Oct note is kept as dated history.

Two texts fixed: Stonkfly's learning-rule description, and the DOOMFLY announcement video card (the clause about read-out cells "chosen because they responded to the screen" is not in the cited files).

Controls ledger (12 Oct 2026): 50 studies, 41 with a wiring null: helps 19, no difference 9, worse 4, mixed 8, not yet scored 1. One row joined, from the authors' own numbers, scored only by our fixed rules: duth-x-stepmania: the authors compared the real wiring with 3 degree-preserving rewired copies (mean) on StepMania hit rate on the 152-note Edit chart. Real 0.9737, null 0.4013 (3 null samples). Our ledger rules read this as helps. Quality: fair, moderate; one seed; the readout groups are taken from the real wiring; 3 rewired copies.

New report: fourteenth check (12 Oct 2026), with the flyvis steps and measurements, the 10-entry re-check, the new ledger row, admissions, triage, tracking and limits.

Controls ledger (11 Oct 2026): 49 studies, 40 with a wiring null: helps 18, no difference 9, worse 4, mixed 8, not yet scored 1. Five rows joined, from the authors' own numbers, scored only by our fixed rules: fly-distill: the authors compared the real wiring with a degree-preserving shuffle on bits per byte (lower is better). Real 3.9572, null 3.9171 (4 null samples). Our ledger rules read this as mixed. flywire-connectome (the author's mushroom-body rate model): the authors compared the real wiring with strength-preserving null wirings (median of 100) on odour discrimination d'. Real 18.32, null 19.45 (100 null samples). Our ledger rules read this as worse. brainlab: the authors compared the real wiring with a target-permuted copy on held-out decision accuracy (%). Real 92.91, null 92.20 (1 null sample). Our ledger rules read this as no-difference. MelanoGraph: the authors compared the real wiring with a degree-preserving rewired copy on the receiver's gain over a resampled message. Real 0.4941, null 0 (1 null sample). Our ledger rules read this as helps. fly-arithmetic: the authors compared the real wiring with a random network of the same size on held-out addition accuracy (%). Real 48, null 98 (10 null samples). Our ledger rules read this as worse. Quality: fly-distill fair, strong; flywire-connectome partly fair, strong; brainlab partly fair, weak; MelanoGraph partly fair, weak; fly-arithmetic partly fair, strong.

Catalogue flag changes (11 Oct 2026): fly-distill no-difference to mixed; flywire-connectome-scz mixed to worse (task metric only); brainlab not-tested to no-difference (a task metric was found in its committed results; its trained_class is now whole-network-or-per-synapse).

Catalogue (11 Oct 2026): 132 entries, 4 new, each graded from code: MelanoGraph (A, ledger row helps), fly-arithmetic (A, ledger row worse), FlyRoyale (B, no results committed) and connectome-control-exploration (B, lesion and input controls only). Project claims are quoted from their READMEs.

Does it actually run? (11 Oct 2026): fly-arithmetic's website ran in our headless Chromium 154 without a GPU and with no action from us; first activity after about 11.2 s, about 2.05 MB; where it computes is unclear; we did not type a sum. 9 of 12 checked demos have run.

Is it real? (11 Oct 2026): the plain answer about suffering is now titled "Is the fly being tortured? Can it suffer? Is it alive or conscious?", with the same sourced answer. For AI agents: release date, release id and current counts first, plus a one-line description of Digital Fly Lab. Build your own, Use in class: a dated note that the drosophila.io home page shows token and wallet text (not reviewed by us).
New report: thirteenth check (11 Oct 2026), with every ledger number and source line, admissions, triage, view counts, the browser check and limits.

Our flyvis layout test (made by us, pre-registered, 10 Oct 2026): does the real wiring layout help a trained fly vision model see which way things move? Not decided: the test did not run, because it needed more memory than our shared machine has. A pre-registered setup check also failed, so no result would have been read. One short simulation of the 45,669-cell model was stopped three times for lack of memory (peak about 3.0 of 3 GiB); the next attempt (planned run 14) needs a leaner simulation loop. We did not retrain the model after shuffling. A model trained on the shuffled wiring might do better, so this asks a narrower question: does this trained model depend on the real layout? A dated note in the sensory part of Does fly wiring help?; no chart, no ledger row.

Catalogue (10 Oct 2026): 128 entries, 3 new, all grade A, each with its own real-versus-shuffled comparison: fly-distill (no difference from shuffled wiring; a random graph did best), flywire-connectome-scz (mushroom-body model on BANC; mixed, 95.3% vs 95.7%, right side only) and brainlab (only activity differs, about 3.7 times the spikes; no task). Their rows join the controls ledger in a later check; the ledger stays at 44 studies.

Correction: Fly With Me's "Is it AI?" class changes from none to whole-network-or-per-synapse (grade B unchanged): at commit 89b130d its server loads 9,978 trained synapses onto 25 descending neurons by default, contrary to a line in its TRAINING.md. 55 of 94 graded projects now have a trained, learning or search-tuned part.

New research report of 10 Oct 2026: the flyvis test step by step (install, setup checks, memory), the 3 new entries, tracking and limits.

Which relays carry the turn? Read by firing rate (our own pre-registered test, brain only, 9 Oct 2026): silencing the relays lowered the turn command to about 60-70% of normal, but silencing random active neurons also moved it, so this is not yet specific to the relays. Silencing other active neurons also changed the turn command, so this relay result is not specific to the relay neurons. With one relay neuron (PVLP141) silenced, the turn command fell to about 70% (left eye) / 65% (right eye) of normal (3 runs per eye). With the 17 (left eye) / 20 (right eye) relay neurons that excite the turn neuron silenced, the turn command fell to about 65% (left eye) / 60% (right eye) of normal (3 runs per eye). The left eye's normal range is only 1 Hz wide (24-25 Hz) and the random control is one draw per eye. Caveat in the chart: One model (Shiu et al. LIF on FlyWire v783), brain only; the input is a rate we set for every LC4/LPLC2 of one eye, not a measured response to a real shadow; 'silenced' means the neuron's output synapses were removed; the normal range comes from 3 runs per eye; not a real fly. The chart replaces the 8 Oct disclosure; the 8 Oct sentences stay only with the label "by the left/right contrast (8 Oct)".
